basics.notice: Listen to each mark: the open a of مَ, the rounded u of دُ, the i of بِ, the closed لْ, and the doubled بِّ.

istiadha.notice: Listen to the words that open every recitation: فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ, then the بسملة.

tabii.notice: Listen to the ا in قَالَ and the و in يَقُولُ: each is held for exactly two counts, twice a short vowel.

arid.notice: Listen to the end of ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ when the reciter stops: the ي before the last letter stretches longer than a normal مد.

iwad.notice: Listen to the stop on أَفْوَاجًا: the تنوين is dropped and the word ends on a two-count ا.

lam-q.notice: Listen to the ل in ٱلْحَمْدُ and ٱلْقَمَرُ: it is said clearly, with سكون, before the next letter.

lam-s.notice: Listen to ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ and ٱلشَّمْسِ: the ل of ال is silent and the next letter is doubled.

ibtida.notice: Listen to how the reciter starts on a word with ٱ, and how the ٱ disappears when he joins it to the word before.

tafkhim.notice: Listen to the ق in ٱلْقَارِعَةُ and the خ in خَلَقَ: the mouth fills and the sound is full and deep.

lam-jh.notice: Listen to the ل of the name in قَالَ ٱللَّهُ: after a فتحة it is heavy and full.

lam-jl.notice: Listen to the ل of the name in بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ: after a كسرة it is light and thin.

ghunnah.notice: Listen to the نّ in إِنَّ and the مّ in ثُمَّ: a nasal hum is held for two counts.

izhar.notice: Listen to the ن in أَنْعَمْتَ: it is said clearly and the tongue moves straight on to the throat letter, with no held hum.

idgh-g.notice: Listen to مَن يَقُولُ: the ن disappears into the ي and a two-count غنة carries it.

idgh-n.notice: Listen to مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ: the ن merges into the ر completely, with no غنة at all.

iqlab.notice: Listen to مِنۢ بَعْدِ: the ن turns into a hidden م on the lips, with a two-count غنة before the ب.

ikhfa.notice: Listen to the ن in مِن قَبْلِكَ: it is hidden, and a soft غنة carries the sound into the ق.

qal-s.notice: Listen to the قْ in وَيَقْطَعُونَ: a small bounce as the letter is released, in the middle of the word.

qal-k.notice: Listen to the stop on ٱلْفَلَقِ: the ق at the end bounces more strongly than in the middle of a word.

muttasil.notice: Listen to جَآءَ: the ا before the همزة in the same word is held four or five counts.

munfasil.notice: Listen to إِنَّآ أَعْطَيْنَٰكَ: the ا at the end of one word is held long before the همزة that starts the next.

mithlayn.notice: Listen to ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ: the two ب become one doubled ب, with no break between them.

mutajanisayn.notice: Listen to قَد تَّبَيَّنَ: the د is not said; it becomes the ت, which is doubled.

sakinayn.notice: Listen to فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ: the ى is not said and فِ runs straight into the ل.

m-izhar.notice: Listen to the مْ in أَلَمْ تَرَ: the lips close once, cleanly, with no held hum.

m-idgham.notice: Listen to كَم مِّن: the two م become one doubled م with a two-count غنة.

m-ikhfa.notice: Listen to تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍ: the م before ب is hidden with a held غنة on the lips.

silent-letters.notice: Listen to ءَامَنُوا۟ and أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ: the letters marked ۟ are written but never said.

silah-s.notice: Listen to إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ: the هـ of the pronoun is stretched into a two-count و between two vowels.

silah-k.notice: Listen to مَالَهُۥٓ أَخْلَدَهُۥ: the pronoun's و is held four or five counts before the همزة.

badal.notice: Listen to ءَامَنُوا۟: the ا after the همزة is only two counts, though a همزة is next to it.

lin.notice: Listen to the stop on قُرَيْشٍ: the يْ after a فتحة is stretched softly before the last letter.

ra-h.notice: Listen to the ر in رَبِّ and مَرْيَمَ: full and heavy, like the heavy letters.

ra-l.notice: Listen to the ر in رِجَالٌ and فِرْعَوْنَ: thin and light, after or with a كسرة.

aqwa-maddayn.notice: Listen to وَلَآ ءَآمِّينَ: the ا after the همزة is held six counts, because the شدة after it is the stronger cause.

dad-zha.notice: Listen to أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ: the ض runs along the side of the tongue, then the ظ comes from the tip at the teeth.

lazim-k.notice: Listen to ٱلضَّآلِّينَ: the ا before the شدة is held a full six counts, joined or stopping.

lazim-h.notice: Listen to the letter names in الٓمٓ: لام and ميم are each held six counts.

mutaqaribayn.notice: Listen to وَقُل رَّبِّ: the ل is not said and the ر is doubled.

waqf-signs.notice: Listen for where the reciter pauses inside a long ayah: the small signs above the line tell him where.

waqf-how.notice: Listen to the last word before each stop: its final vowel becomes a سكون, and a ة becomes a soft هـ.

rawm-ishmam.notice: Listen to the stop on نَسْتَعِينُ: a trace of the ضمة can be heard (الروم), or the lips round with no sound (الإشمام).

sakt.notice: Listen to مَنْ ۜ رَاقٍ: the voice stops for a moment with no breath, so the ن stays clear instead of merging into the ر.

imalah.notice: Listen to مَجْر۪ىٰهَا: the ا leans toward an e sound, the only such word in حفص.

ishmam.notice: Listen to تَأْمَ۫نَّا: the lips round briefly on the first ن before the merged doubled ن.

tashil.notice: Listen to ءَا۬عْجَمِىٌّ: the second همزة is softened, between a همزة and an ا.

makharij-jawf.notice: Listen to بَا، بُو، بِي: the long vowels come from the open space of the mouth and throat, with no contact.

makharij-halq.notice: Listen to أَءْ، أَهْ، أَعْ، أَحْ، أَغْ، أَخْ: each starts at a different depth of the throat.

makharij-aqsa.notice: Listen to أَقْ and أَكْ: the back of the tongue touches the palate, ق further back than ك.

makharij-wasat.notice: Listen to أَجْ، أَشْ، أَيْ and أَضْ: the middle and the side of the tongue at work.

makharij-taraf.notice: Listen to أَلْ، أَنْ، أَرْ and أَتْ، أَدْ، أَطْ: each made with the tip of the tongue at a slightly different spot.

makharij-shafatan.notice: Listen to أَفْ، أَبْ، أَمْ، أَوْ: the lips, and the hum from the nose in م and ن.

sifat-hams.notice: Listen to أَفْ and أَبْ: a flow of breath with the first, the breath held back with the second.

sifat-shidda.notice: Listen to أَبْ, أَلْ and أَسْ: the sound stops, half-flows, or runs freely.

sifat-istila.notice: Listen to أَصْ and أَسْ: the same place, but the tongue rises and covers in ص.

sifat-safir.notice: Listen to أَصْ، أَزْ، أَسْ: a whistle runs through the front teeth.

sifat-inhiraf.notice: Listen to أَرْ and أَشْ: the ر trembles once, no more; the ش spreads through the mouth.

maratib.notice: Listen to the same ayah at three speeds: every length and غنة stays, only the pace changes.
